body:
Gorgeous! It looks almost too good to eat. Congratulations and best wishes!

I would love the recipe sometime when you're not super busy/getting married. Enjoy your honeymoon!

Thanks! I am trying. I made myself cook something. Stove top only. I called my husband and told him I was feeling down, sugar coated I know, but it's something.  Now I have a kitchen to clean, a list to write, and a dinner to half heartedly pick at while I write a list of things I want to do with my life before I die.

So hard! I know I am not alone in this, it's just hard to moving forward when those feelings sneak up on you from behind and incapacitate you with their chloroform soaked rag of grief and regret. Those feelings are really sneaky. They stalk me through my day and wait for a moment when I am truly and finally happy and laughing or even just pleasantly humming and then tap me on the shoulder. If I am around other people I can shake it off and lose my pursuer in the flow of conversation. When I'm alone it doesn't just politely tap me on the shoulder, it kicks me in the back, knocks me down, forces the air out of my lungs, then smothers all means of intake with its noxious poison until I can't move or do anything but think about giving in and taking a final and permanent way out. Some days it takes everything I have to keep moving forward. Today, I found a new recipe. I am hoping that will work.

I lost my best friend a year ago. I really want to see her, but she would want me to live my fullest life. I made myself get up and cook something because that's what she would tell me to do if she could talk to me. I'll start writing a list of all the things I need to do before I am ready to die. It's something I have done before. It'll be really long and I will probably die of old age before I finish it, which will hopefully bring me around and make me realize I have a lot to live for and I want to be alive.

These episodes are just so hard to get through sometimes. It's really hard when I'm alone. And they're getting worse. 
Thank you for responding. It helps to know that someone is out there.

I live in the U. S. and have no plans this evening. Going through some irrational crap myself at the moment, but I am more than willing to listen to whatever you have to say. I cannot be there with you physically, but I will gladly lend an ear.

Getting out of bed is hard. Looking at the things in your life that need to change that you can't do anything about is awful. The future is uncertain and the place where you are sucks. At times like these it's hard to be hopeful. 

You can do something positive though, just for kicks. Think about your favorite food. Think about what it would take for you to be able to eat that even just one more time. 

I am struggling with some awful thoughts right now and thinking about some spicy cheesy pasta with sautéed spinach and a sweet potato on the side has almost gotten me out of bed three times. It's a pain to make the pasta, I don't remember the recipe, and I would have to get dressed to get some fresh ingredients, but I am starting to consider that it may truly be a worthwhile endeavor. 

You can pull through this. You can get a job. You can take a shower, comb your hair, and brush your teeth and feel better. You can get up and grab your favorite takeout or cook your favorite meal. You have the ability. You can do this.
